Set beneath the Chyulu Hills with Mount Kilimanjaro views, Finch Hattons is a luxury safari camp in Tsavo West, Kenya s largest and oldest national park. It offers a safari experience that goes far beyond twice daily game drives, from volcanic landscapes and natural springs to Maasai cultural experiences, rich birdlife, quiet wilderness and restorative wellness. With just 17 tented suites, it is an exquisite blend of old-world safari romance, adventure and stillness, wrapped in genuine Kenyan hospitality.
Recognised among the Best 100 Hotels in Africa at the Tatler Best Africa Awards 2026
Voted one of Travel + Leisure's 500 Best Hotels 2025
Discover the highlights
Tented Suites
Elevated above natural springs, the 17 luxury tented suites at Finch Hattons are designed for privacy, comfort and a front-row-seat to the rhythm of Tsavo. Wake to birdsong, watch hippos bathe below your deck and settle into the romance of safari life, where old-world elegance meets considered comfort and every thoughtful detail is beautifully taken care of.
Read more
Beyond game drives
Game drives are only the beginning. Walk through ancient cloud forest in the Chyulu Hills, explore the Shetani Lava Flows, enjoy bush breakfasts, meet the Maasai community of Iltilal or head out after dark on a night drive. From natural springs and rhino encounters to wide-open skies, Finch Hattons reveals Tsavo West in all its wild, uncrowded beauty.

FAQs
Frequently asked questions
Looking for answers?
Find answers to our most frequently asked questions about staying at Finch Hattons.
Location & Travel
Why should I visit Tsavo West?
Tsavo National Park, located in Kenya's southeastern corner, is one of the largest national parks in the world and one of the country's best-kept safari secrets. Split into two distinct regions - Tsavo East and Tsavo West - the park offers a raw, untouched safari experience for nature enthusiasts, adventurers, and travelers seeking solace away from the crowds.
Tsavo East is known for its iconic red-dust plains and free-roaming elephant herds, while Tsavo West is defined by dramatic volcanic landscapes, ancient lava flows, and the Chyulu Hills, which offer sweeping views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Natural springs across the park feed a landscape rich in birdlife, supporting one of Kenya's most diverse ecosystems.
With significantly fewer visitors than parks like the Maasai Mara, Tsavo offers a more intimate, uncrowded luxury safari experience in Kenya, one where wellness and stillness are as much a part of the journey as the wildlife itself.
Find out more here .
Why should I visit Kenya for a safari?
Kenya is the birthplace of the safari, and it’s not hard to see why. With its vast open plains teeming with wildlife, this country is truly magical, and visitors will often spot lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and African buffaloes – also known as the Big Five – within the first few days of their stay.
How do I get to Finch Hattons?
The main international airport in Nairobi is Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, with daily direct flights from the main European hubs: London, Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam, as well as New York. There are also daily arrivals from Johannesburg in South Africa, as well as from hubs in the Middle East, including Dubai and Doha. Flights from Europe take, on average, just over 8 hours, and direct flights from New York take 15 hours.
Those connecting from any other USA hub will need to travel via one of the cities above. We can also book the Fast Track service for you at the Jomo Kenyatta Airport to speed up your journey. Our reservations team can help organise transfers to and from the airports.
Daily scheduled flights from Wilson Airport (WIL) in Nairobi take just 50 minutes to reach our private airstrip in Tsavo, operated by our trusted partners, Safarilink and Fly ALS. Or, if you’re flying from Mombasa, Mombasa Air also offers direct flights to our airstrip. Once you land, it’s only a quick 10-minute drive to Finch Hattons.
Can Finch Hattons help arrange my travel and book my stay?
Yes. Finch Hattons' reservations team can book your stay and arrange your travel within Kenya ahead of your trip, including internal flights from Nairobi's Wilson Airport to the camp's private airstrip in Tsavo (a 50-minute flight) and airport transfers to and from camp. Finch Hattons does not book international flights to Kenya, so these are arranged directly with an airline. Once you've landed in Kenya, the reservations team takes care of the rest, so all you need to do is arrive.
Does Finch Hattons offer airport transfers?
Yes, the team at Finch Hattons can arrange transfers between international and domestic airports for arrivals from outside Kenya.
What are the baggage restrictions?
The luggage limit on the flights from Wilson Airport to Finch Hattons is 15kg, which includes your hand luggage. This is quite strictly enforced as the aircraft used doesn’t have a lot of extra space. It’s advisable to pack in soft-sided or duffel bags as they tend to be more flexible and easier to fit into the aircraft’s limited storage compartments.
If you’re on a longer trip and have additional luggage, you can usually leave this at the terminal free of charge until you return.
Please check with your airline before departing. At the other end, when you land at the private airstrip, our team will collect you in Finch Hattons vehicles for the 10-minute transfer to the camp.
What is the currency in Kenya and will I need cash?
The currency is the Kenyan Shilling and is readily accepted for both large and small transactions. You may need at least USD 50 in cash per person to pay for your entry visa if you’ve not organised this prior to arrival.
The airport authorities accept payment in Euros and British Pounds however amounts may vary, and they are less likely to have the exact change. Credit cards are not accepted. ATMs are available at the main international airport and in larger towns; however, they can struggle to process non-Kenyan cards.
We recommend obtaining some Shillings before you depart for small purchases while you’re in transit (or if you plan on spending any time in Nairobi).
At Finch Hattons, you will not need any cash. Purchases from the gift shop or spa treatments can be made by credit card.
Will I need any vaccinations for a Kenya safari?
No vaccinations are required on entry unless you have just arrived from countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission. Malaria is still a risk in some areas of Kenya, so it is important to seek medical advice on appropriate precautions during your stay.
Will I require a visa for Kenya?
Entry requirements for Kenya vary depending on your nationality and the purpose and length of your stay. Most international visitors are required to obtain a Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) before travelling, while certain nationalities may be exempt.
